intro.title: Streams
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple file processing application that reads a large text file and writes a transformed version to a new file. You will learn the core concept of streams in Node.js, which allow you to handle data in chunks efficiently without loading entire files into memory. The main technologies involved are the built-in Node.js 'fs' module and its 'createReadStream' and 'createWriteStream' methods. By the end, you'll understand how to use readable and writable streams to process data piece by piece, making your applications more performant and scalable.
intro.usecase: Streams are fundamental in Node.js for handling large files and data flows efficiently, such as when processing video uploads on platforms like YouTube or Netflix, where files are too large to load entirely into memory. They enable real-time data processing in applications like log monitoring tools or financial trading platforms, where data arrives continuously and needs immediate analysis. Streams also power features like live chat in messaging apps, where messages are transmitted and displayed as they're received without waiting for complete transmission. As a developer, you'll use streams to build scalable applications that handle I/O operations without blocking the event loop, crucial for high-performance web servers and data processing pipelines.
